newsitem.title: USA: Countrymark opposes CBOT corn, soy delivery plan.
newsitem.headline: Countrymark opposes CBOT corn, soy delivery plan.

text.p: Another prominent eastern Corn Belt merchandiser, Countrymark Co-op, has issued a strong statement opposing the Chicago Board of Trade's proposed delivery changes for its corn and soybean contracts.
"Frankly, only one group of people benefit from the proposal presumably, the traders on the CBOT," said Countrymark Co-op chief executive David Swanson in a statement issued on Friday.
"Farmers, feeders, processors and the entire agriculture community would be damaged by this proposed change," he said.
CBOT members will vote on the proposed changes April 15.
Ohio-based merchandiser The Andersons Inc issued a statement last month saying the proposals were "alarming" and needed to be revised.

The plan, developed by a CBOT Task Force, eliminates both St Louis and Toledo as delivery locations of CBOT corn and soybeans and replaces them with delivery at elevators on the Illinois River between Peoria and Chicago, including Burns Harbor, Ind.
"There is absolutely no reason to close Toledo until the Illinois River idea has an opportunity to be tested," Countrymark's Swanson said.
Countrymark Co-op is based in Indianapolis. Both Countrymark Co-op and The Andersons have large grain storage facilities in the Toledo area.

The Andersons own about 25 million bushels of elevator space in the Toledo area. Toledo's seven delivery elevators currently represent 70 percent of the 79 million bushels of delivery space in Chicago, St Louis and Toledo.

"I do not understand the urgency to make this change on such short notice which does not allow for adequate public debate," Gary Anderson, president and CEO of The Andersons, said in a statement last month.

"Making delivery solely along the Illinois River is alarming. The majority of the river facilities can only load barges. That's a problem if the river freezes or floods or if something happens downstream with the river locks," he said.

The Commodity Futures Trading Commission, which in December 1996 told the CBOT that its traditional system for cash deliveries needed to be changed due to shrinking Chicago elevator space, is taking public comments on the CBOT plan until April 15, the same date as the CBOT members' vote.
